title: Adaptive KV Residency Orchestrator and Continuous Batcher Tuning for Varied Prompt/Response Distributions
creator: Amara Singh
description:
Background: Mixed prompt/response workloads in production (short prompts + long streamed responses, multi-turn chat and API call mixing) cause KV cache churn and GPU slab fragmentation. Continuous batcher heuristics currently prioritize fill rate and average latency, which leads to KV eviction hotspots for long-running responses and suboptimal tail latency for short interactive queries.

Goal: Design and implement an adaptive KV residency orchestrator paired with continuous-batcher tuning that: (1) predicts per-request slot tenure and pins hot KV ranges to reduce eviction churn; (2) favors low-latency short requests during congestion while maintaining throughput for long responses; (3) reduces GPU memory fragmentation and lowers 95th/99th percentile latency without increasing steady-state cost.

Constraints: Must be compatible with existing runtime kernel-selection and should not require offline model changes. Changes should be feature-flagged and observable via the Console. Target rollout must support Canary -> A/B -> Gradual rollout with automatic fallback to current policy on regressions.

High-level approach: Introduce a lightweight KV Residency Orchestrator that runs alongside the continuous batcher. Core components: (a) Tenure predictor: online estimator that uses request metadata (length, streaming flag, historical token emission) to predict expected number of KV blocks required for the request lifetime; (b) Residency planner: maps predicted tenure to an action (pin, soft-pin with LRU weight, prefetch) per KV shard; (c) Batcher policy adjuster: temporarily relaxes coalescing thresholds for short requests under contention and elevates eviction buffer for pinned KV to avoid premature eviction. We will also expose per-GPU slab watermarks and peer-facing debug metrics.

Metrics and success criteria: primary metrics are tail latencies (p95/p99 gen latency), token throughput (tokens/sec), GPU memory fragmentation ratio, and eviction rate per-minute. Target improvements (canary threshold): p95 reduced by >=10% on mixed workloads, eviction rate reduced by >=25% during steady-state spikes, fragmentation ratio reduced by >=12% on synthetic skew tests.

Trade-offs considered: aggressive pinning reduces eviction churn but increases residency pressure; we mitigate by soft-pin weight decay and dynamic slab-reservation heuristics. Prefetching improves warm-start latencies for long responses but can increase memory footprint; prefetch will be constrained to a configurable budget per-GPU.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Notes: This ticket focuses on runtime-side orchestration and scheduler tuning; separate follow-up will evaluate model-side prompt shaping hints and client-side rate-limiting policies.
tasks: Design KV Residency Orchestrator API and feature flag schema
Implement Tenure Predictor using online exponential smoothing and request metadata
Implement Residency Planner and integrate with KV manager (pin / soft-pin / prefetch ops)
Add batcher policy hooks: coalescing threshold override and short-request priority lane
Expose metrics and tracing: per-request predicted-tenure, pin decisions, eviction traces
Run synthetic benchmarks (mixed short/long, chat-like) and capture baselines
Canary rollout with controlled traffic and rollback hooks
Ship documentation and Console dashboard panels for the feature

Eviction rate reduced >=25% during steady spikes in canary traffic
